tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a clean stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the largest disk to the target, and finally recursively move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have a contiguous stack of disks on a single peg that need to be moved as a unit to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, verify that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk you intend to move and that the move does not place a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever generating a move, check that the move respects the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where the top disk is 2, resulting in moving a non‑top disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without breaking the size rule, so use it to temporarily hold space and enable moving larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk’s source or target peg is blocked by smaller disks, move the smallest disk to a free peg to create space.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Skipping the move of the smallest disk and trying to place a larger disk onto a smaller one, causing a size violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the final tower’s larger disks in the correct order, keep them in place and only move the remaining disks onto them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has a partial correct stack, avoid moving those disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a correctly placed larger disk away from the goal peg, breaking the final order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto the goal peg once its smaller disks are cleared.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When building the final stack, start with the largest disk and work downwards, moving each disk onto the goal after clearing smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a smaller disk before the larger one, leading to later illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, output it as the last syntactically correct list in the response, ensuring the verifier can parse it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of solution generation, make sure the move list is the final parseable list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including extra text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the final list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear source and auxiliary pegs before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you want to move has any smaller disks on top of it (source peg) or the auxiliary peg you intend to use, first move those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk, ensure its source peg has it on top and the auxiliary peg is free of smaller disks that would block the move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 while disk 2 remains on top of it, resulting in moving a non‑top disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg before placing a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto its final peg, ensure that the target peg does not have any smaller disks on top that would be violated by the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, verify that the peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg where disk 1 is on top, violating size ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Alternate smallest-disk moves with the only other legal move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After each move of the smallest disk, make the only possible legal move that does not involve the smallest disk; repeat this alternating pattern. This systematic approach guarantees progress and avoids dead ends in the Tower of Hanoi with arbitrary configurations.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When solving a Tower of Hanoi puzzle where disks are distributed across pegs, use this alternating move pattern to decide each step.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while the smallest disk is not positioned to free the source or target, leading to an illegal move or a stuck configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the move list short enough to fit within the model’s output token budget and avoid truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list for a Tower of Hanoi problem, especially with larger numbers of disks, aim for a minimal or compact sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing an excessively long move list that gets cut off, resulting in an incomplete answer.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget to include the final move list or think it has already output it earlier.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly output the move list as the last syntactically correct list, ensuring it is not empty.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may not check the size rule when selecting a move.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the target peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may select a disk that is not the topmost on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the top disk of its source peg before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated answer exceeds the token limit or the model stops early, cutting off the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise; ensure the final answer ends with a complete list; monitor token usage.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of disk locations during reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit representation of the current configuration and verify the source peg contains the disk before moving.
